Report_ID: Penta-3 completion at 18 weeks of age
Title: Automated phone call and text reminders for childhood immunisations (PRIMM): a randomised controlled trial in Nigeria
Author: Ekhaguere et al.
Comment: The analysis is explicitly labelled modified intention-to-treat rather than conventional intention-to-treat. It retains all 300 randomized participants in each arm regardless of where immunisation was received or how it was audited, despite reported deaths and loss to follow-up. The paper reports rounded percentages (81% and 86%); raw events and randomized totals were extracted directly. No cluster adjustment is required because randomization was individual.
Design Type: Two-arm parallel individually randomized controlled trial
Study Environment: Mother and Child Hospitals in semi-rural Ondo State
Medium: Automated SMS text messages and voice calls
Content length: Voice-call reminder duration was 50 s; SMS length was not stated
Topic of Content: Reminder of the child's upcoming immunisation visit and the protective value of immunisation
interaction_type: Automated one-way reminders sent 2 days and 1 day before scheduled vaccination
Recruitment source: Postpartum wards at Mother and Child Hospital Ondo Town and Mother and Child Hospital Akure
Outcome measurement: Receipt of Penta-1, Penta-2, and Penta-3 by 18 weeks, ascertained from immunisation clinic record books and the mid-study phone survey
Outcome variable: Penta-3 completion at 18 weeks of age
outcome_family: receipt of the third dose of a DTP-containing vaccine

Title: SMS text message reminders to improve infant vaccination coverage in Guatemala: A pilot randomized controlled trial
Author: Domek et al.
Comment: The arm-level events and totals are crude intention-to-treat data and are suitable for calculating a review-level risk ratio. The paper did not report a risk ratio, so no RR was entered. The reported p-value (0.69) is adjusted for income and should not replace the crude event-count synthesis. Immunization records could only be confirmed for children who returned to one of the two study sites.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention: SMS reminders plus usual written reminders') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Individually randomized two-arm parallel-group pilot randomized controlled trial
Study Environment: Two public health clinics in Guatemala City serving a publicly insured and low-income population
Content length: Three SMS reminders at six, four, and two days before the scheduled dates for visits 2 and 3
Topic of Content: Reminder that the child was due for vaccines, including the child's name, scheduled date, and clinic name
Participant type: Parents or caregivers of infants aged 8–14 weeks presenting for the first dose of the primary immunization series
Recruitment source: Two public health clinics in Guatemala City
Outcome measurement: Completion of all 3 pentavalent doses; vaccination records confirmed for children returning to either study clinic
outcome_family: receipt of the third dose of a DTP-containing vaccine

Title: Providing mothers with mobile phone message reminders increases childhood immunization and vitamin A supplementation coverage in Côte d’Ivoire: A randomized controlled trial
Author: Dissieka et al.
Comment: The table also reports an adjusted odds ratio of 2.68 (95% CI 1.84-3.91) and P<0.001, but these were intentionally not used for the planned crude risk-ratio synthesis. The paper states the inequality P<0.001 rather than an exact p value, so p_value is left null. No risk ratio was reported by the paper; it should be calculated downstream from the extracted crude event counts and totals. study_year records the explicitly stated trial start year; recruitment continued through June 2015.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention group: SMS or voice reminder messages') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Individually randomized, two-arm controlled trial with block randomization by health-facility location
Study Environment: 29 public-sector health facilities in Korhogo district
Medium: SMS text message or automated voice message delivered by mobile phone
Content length: One reminder two days before the scheduled visit and up to two additional reminders after non-attendance
Topic of Content: Reminder to take the child for immunization to protect the child's health
Participant type: Mother/caretaker-child pairs; infants enrolled at the BCG visit
Recruitment source: 29 health facilities in Korhogo district during the child's BCG immunization visit

Title: Effect of Mobile Phone Text Message Reminders on Routine Immunization Uptake in Pakistan: Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Kazi et al.
Comment: Crude ITT counts were extracted as required. The paper did not report a risk ratio, so no RR was calculated or entered. The narrative states P<.31, while Table 3 reports P=.31; the table value was used. Vaccination status was card-verified for 69.3% of participants and verbally reported for the remainder.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention: standard counseling plus one-way SMS reminders') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Individually randomized two-arm parallel-group controlled trial
Study Environment: Urban squatter settlement in an HDSS catchment area
Medium: Automated one-way SMS text messages to caregivers' mobile phones
Content length: Four SMS reminders during the week the child was due for the 14-week EPI vaccination
Topic of Content: Reminder that the named child was due for vaccination and should be taken immediately to the nearest EPI center
Participant type: Infants less than 2 weeks old at enrollment and their parents or caregivers
Recruitment source: Households of newborns in the Ibrahim Haidry health demographic surveillance system catchment area
Outcome measurement: Vaccination status documented at the 18-week household follow-up; records were verified by physically examining EPI immunization cards when available
outcome_family: receipt of the third dose of a DTP-containing vaccine

Title: Mobile phone-delivered reminders and incentives to improve childhood immunisation coverage and timeliness in Kenya (M-SIMU): a cluster randomised controlled trial
Author: Gibson et al.
Comment: These are crude counts among the modified intention-to-treat analytic sample with documented 12-month MCH booklet data, not all randomised participants. Enrolled totals were control n=489 and SMS-only n=476, but all-randomised Pentavalent-3 event counts were not reported; do not pair the reported events with enrolled denominators. The reported RR 0.98 (95% CI 0.96–1.01) and p=0.20 were not entered in numeric effect fields because they are GEE cluster-adjusted, whereas the synthesis contract prioritises crude event counts. Villages were the randomisation units (38 per arm); no Pentavalent-3-specific ICC or design effect was reported.; excluded by outcome classification: does not match the requested outcome/timepoint (meta_analysis_candidate=False)
Study Environment: Rural community and immunisation-clinic catchment setting in Gem and Asembo districts, western Kenya
Topic of Content: Reminders before scheduled pentavalent and measles immunisation visits
interaction_type: One-way automated reminder messages to caregivers
Recruitment source: Infant-caregiver pairs identified at home through the KEMRI/CDC Health and Demographic Surveillance System village reporters
Outcome measurement: Written immunisation records in the child’s maternal and child health booklet at 12-month follow-up
additional_group_ns: SMS plus 75 KES (n=446); SMS plus 200 KES (n=406); excluded because reminders were combined with monetary incentives
outcome_family: receipt of the third dose of a DTP-containing vaccine

Report_ID: Immunization coverage at 14 weeks for Penta3
Title: Effectiveness of short message services reminder on childhood immunization programme in Kadoma, Zimbabwe - a randomized controlled trial, 2013
Author: Bangure et al.
Comment: The paper reports p < 0.001; p_value stores the stated threshold, not an exact p value. Exact vaccinated counts are not reported. Although the synthesis prompt pre-identifies 144/152 and 114/152 by applying the displayed percentages to randomized denominators, the intervention count is not uniquely recoverable: both 144/152 (94.7%) and 145/152 (95.4%) can display as 95% after whole-percent rounding. Therefore event counts are left null under the anti-hallucination rule. The coverage statement combines OPV3, Penta3 and PCV3, but explicitly includes Penta3. The paper's stated 1.3-times relative comparison is recorded in the general risk-ratio bucket; no confidence interval for that ratio is reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('SMS reminders plus routine health education') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Individually randomized two-arm parallel-group controlled trial
Content length: Three reminders before each appointment: 7 days, 3 days, and 1 day before
Recruitment source: Kadoma City clinics after delivery or during the 3rd- and 7th-day post-delivery visits
Outcome measurement: Immunization coverage at 14 weeks, assessed through telephone follow-up and comparison with clinic immunization registers
Outcome variable: Immunization coverage at 14 weeks for Penta3
outcome_family: receipt of the third dose of a DTP-containing vaccine
